editions.intro: Good afternoon, and welcome to your Baseline briefing. It is a quieter week on the tours, with smaller events in Ningbo and Brussels, but there is still plenty of news as the season heads into its final stretch.

stories.title: Iga Swiatek ends her 2026 season after thigh injury
stories.summary: Iga Swiatek has brought her season to a close. The Polish star, currently number nine in the world, told fans on Instagram that she needs a longer spell of rest to recover properly from a problem with her left thigh, which troubled her during last week's semi-final defeat to Maja Chwalinska in Wuhan. She has already pulled out of Ningbo this week and will also miss Tokyo. Her withdrawal ends any hope of reaching the WTA Finals, and she will not travel as an alternate either. It brings down the curtain on a mixed year that included the title in Toronto in August and a quarter-final run at the Australian Open.

stories.title: Six stars pull out of the Ningbo Open
stories.summary: The WTA 500 event in Ningbo has been hit hard by withdrawals. Alongside Iga Swiatek, world number four Jessica Pegula has stepped aside to focus on her health, Elina Svitolina has withdrawn, Maja Chwalinska says her body needs rest after two demanding weeks, Anna Kalinskaya is unwell, and Wang Xiyu has also pulled out. Of the five top ten players originally due to take part, only two remain. The tournament runs until Sunday the 25th of October, and it is one of the last chances for players to collect ranking points before the WTA Finals.

stories.title: Elena Rybakina sets her sights on finishing the year as world number one
stories.summary: Elena Rybakina, the world number one, says her main aim for the rest of the season is to stay at the top of the rankings until the year is done. She has found wins hard to come by since lifting the US Open title in September, but she is back in action in Ningbo this week, where her opening match in the second round is against Polina Kudermetova. After that she will defend her WTA Finals title, with the season finale being held at Indian Wells for the first time, from the 8th to the 15th of November, having moved from Riyadh.

stories.title: Alex Eala ends her losing run in Ningbo
stories.summary: Alex Eala is back in the winning column. The Filipino, ranked twentieth in the world, beat Diane Parry six-three, six-one in the first round in Ningbo on Monday, her first victory since the US Open after early exits in Singapore and Wuhan. It will be a welcome relief after some harsh criticism from fans during her slump. Next up is a tougher test against the thirteenth seed Diana Shnaider, who came through against Yulia Putintseva after saving five set points. Eala is also on the entry list for the event in Tokyo that follows.

stories.title: Alexander Zverev reaches three hundred weeks in the top five
stories.summary: Alexander Zverev has now spent three hundred weeks inside the top five of the ATP rankings, a mark reached by only a small group of men since computer rankings began in 1973. It is a fitting milestone at the end of a landmark year, because the German is already guaranteed to finish 2026 as world number one. With Jannik Sinner out for the rest of the season with a knee injury, nobody can catch him. Zverev would be the first German man since Boris Becker to end a year at the top. He may adjust his schedule to stay fresh for the Paris Masters and the ATP Finals.

stories.title: Novak Djokovic praised for adding Basel to his schedule
stories.summary: Novak Djokovic has taken a wildcard into the Swiss Indoors in Basel, which runs from the 26th of October to the 1st of November, and Andy Roddick has applauded the move. Speaking on his podcast, Roddick said the extra matches late in the year could set Djokovic up well for another tilt at the Australian Open in January. There is a more immediate prize too. Djokovic sits eleventh in the race to the ATP Finals in Turin and needs to climb into the top nine, so strong runs in Basel and at the Paris Masters will be vital. Djokovic won the Basel title once before, back in 2009.

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz has one last shot at a Masters record in Paris
stories.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has not won a Masters 1000 title this year, and the Paris Masters is his final chance to change that. If he wins it, he would join Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal as the only men to claim a Masters crown in five straight seasons since the format began in 1990. Paris has never suited him, though. He has yet to go beyond the quarter-finals there. His 2026 season has been interrupted by a wrist injury that cost him four and a half months, including Roland Garros and Wimbledon, although he did win the Australian Open, Doha and Tokyo.

stories.title: Zizou Bergs shrugs off Alcaraz's comments as Brussels gets under way
stories.summary: Zizou Bergs has calmly brushed aside Carlos Alcaraz's suggestion that luck played a part in their Shanghai meeting. The Belgian, number forty-one in the world, beat Alcaraz seven-five, seven-six in the third round, his first win over a top three player. Afterwards Alcaraz admitted he played poorly but felt a few frame shots had gone his opponent's way. Bergs says he does not read too much into post-match remarks and is focused on his own progress. He opens his home event in Brussels against Toby Samuel, where the fifth seed Alex Michelsen and Jaume Munar have already reached the second round.

stories.title: Elina Svitolina announces split from Gael Monfils
stories.summary: Elina Svitolina has announced that her marriage to fellow player Gael Monfils is coming to an end. In a heartfelt post on Monday, the Ukrainian said she needs time to find herself again, and that the war at home has affected her deeply. She stressed that nobody is to blame, thanked Monfils for respecting her feelings, and said their daughter Skai will always come first as they continue to raise her together. The couple married in 2021. Svitolina, the world number six, has also withdrawn from Ningbo this week, and she asked fans for kindness and space.

stories.title: Talk turns to Jannik Sinner's next coach
stories.summary: With Darren Cahill expected to step away from Jannik Sinner's team at the end of the year, the guessing game over his successor has begun. Juan Carlos Ferrero, who previously guided Carlos Alcaraz, has said he would be open to the role, while the Italian former player Adriano Panatta has suggested his compatriot Paolo Bertolucci would be the ideal fit. Nothing has been decided. Sinner himself has not played since winning Wimbledon in July and has ended his season early because of a knee problem, with his return now set for 2027.

editions.outro: That is all for this briefing. Enjoy the tennis this week, and we will be back with more soon.
